_readme: Canonical registry of citable WORKS (not individual granthas/editions) for DGE's cross-reference/entity-linking system — see dge/SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md. This is deliberately separate from taxonomy.json (which describes the FOLDER hierarchy of what's actually digitized) and library.json (which catalogs individual digitized editions/commentaries): an entity here is the abstract WORK a citation names ("ब्रह्मसूत्रे", "अष्टाध्याय्याम्"), which the resolver maps to one or more concrete corpus locations. Every part of DGE that needs to recognize a citation or display a canonical work name should read from here, not invent its own alias/label map (the exact anti-pattern that produced the taxonomy label drift documented in SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md's taxonomy-labels section). Display names for the WORK ITSELF (not its citation aliases) still resolve through library.js's DGE_PATH_LABELS/dgeSegLabel for the corpus category, so this file stores the Sanskrit/IAST facts about the work, not a duplicate general-purpose label map.

brahmasutra.notes: Corpus text is Madhva's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya (mūla stratum only); this is the only Brahma Sūtra text presently digitized in DGE, so a bare 'ब्रह्मसूत्रे N.N.N' resolves here regardless of school. Verified against the real data.json: unit ids are 'BS_C01_S01_V02'-shaped (Chapter/Section/Verse), NOT a plain dotted number -- an earlier draft of this registry assumed '{adhyaya}.{pada}.{sutra}' directly, which never matched.

ashtadhyayi.notes: Already has its own dedicated index/page and popover (dge/js/intellisense.js, window.dgeLookupSutra) built earlier in this project — the entity-linker's card reuses that page rather than the generic reader route. This is the SAME sūtra-citation detector's target vocabulary; entity-linker.js generalizes intellisense.js's engine to sources OTHER than the sūtra text itself (e.g. a Nyāya work quoting Pāṇini), rather than replacing it.

rigveda.notes: Verified against dge/data/vedas/rigveda/shakala_shakha/samhita/mandala_01/data.json: each unit's own 'id' field IS the dotted mandala.sukta.rik reference (e.g. "1.1.1"), which core.js's normalizer carries through as vedicId for non-chapter Vedic schemas — no extra lookup table needed.

bhagavata_purana.notes: Chapter-grouped schema (itihasa_purana_text): core.js sets vedicId to chapter.reference + ' · ' + shloka-number, e.g. "Skandha 10, Adhyaya 14 · 8" — verified against dge/data/purana/maha_purana/bhagavata_purana/skandha_10/data.json's adhyaya_01 chapter, whose 'reference' field is literally "Skandha 10, Adhyaya 1". This ONLY resolves correctly after the core.js dgeResolveQuickJumpTarget non-numeric-vedicId fix landed alongside this registry (see SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md) — before that fix every chapter-based vedicId collided on the same broken key.

vishnu_purana.notes: Level 2 (named-work) detection only for tonight's pass — resolves to the work and, when an amsha number is present, to that amsha's grantha. Verse-level (adhyaya/shloka) deep-linking is deferred: this amsha's own chapter-reference string convention hasn't been verified against real data.json yet (see 'Deferred' in SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md).

mahabharata.notes: Level 2 (named-work) only tonight. 18 parvas each need their own route entry (adi_parva shown as the representative landing route) plus a parva-name lookup for numbered citations (e.g. भारते शान्तिपर्वणि) — deferred, see SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md.

ramayana.notes: Level 2 (named-work) only tonight, same reasoning as Mahābhārata — 7 kāṇḍas each need their own route (bāla kāṇḍa shown as representative).

sumadhvavijaya.notes: The exact work the project lead's screenshot searched (कान्ताय → Sumadhvavijaya 1.1, the opening verse of Sarga 1). Included so the same example anchors both the plain-search test case AND the entity-linker's own test data.
